decision_reason: A1 already provides a physically justified gravity-relative ordering for the close static classes, so no unsupported second static-posture distinction is introduced. The main deficiencies are that generic translational_motion does not distinguish horizontal locomotion from the vertical progression characteristic of climbing stairs, jogging differs from walking primarily by intensity, and motion_regularity is constant across all supplied class prototypes. A2 therefore splits translation by gravity-relative direction, adds an airborne-loading-cycle concept to separate gait regimes using running and jump front & back as seen anchors, adds lower-limb motion prominence for sensor-supported body-region transfer, and drops the non-discriminative regularity dimension.

attributes.name: motion_intensity
attributes.definition: Overall magnitude and energy of motion within a window, including both linear and rotational components.

attributes.name: cadence
attributes.definition: Rate at which a meaningful periodic motion unit repeats over time. Cadence measures repetitions per unit time, not the total number of repetitions in the recording.

levels.Low: No clear periodic repetition or a slow repetition rate.

attributes.name: smoothness
attributes.definition: Degree to which motion changes continuously rather than through sustained rapid fluctuations.

levels.Medium: Moderately smooth motion with some fluctuations.
levels.High: Continuous and smooth motion with little fluctuation.

attributes.name: impulsiveness
attributes.definition: Degree to which motion contains short, abrupt, high-magnitude changes or impacts.

levels.Low: Few or no pronounced abrupt peaks.

attributes.name: posture_inclination
attributes.definition: Average gravity-relative inclination of the global load-bearing body configuration within a window, rather than the orientation of an isolated moving limb.

levels.High: Strongly inclined or nearly horizontal relative to gravity.

attributes.name: posture_variability
attributes.definition: Extent to which the global load-bearing body configuration changes relative to gravity within a window, rather than local limb-orientation changes.

attributes.name: rotational_motion
attributes.definition: Prominence of angular or rotational motion during the activity.

attributes.name: horizontal_progression
attributes.definition: Prominence of sustained locomotor translation approximately perpendicular to gravity within a window.

levels.Low: Little or no sustained horizontal progression.

attributes.name: vertical_progression
attributes.definition: Prominence of sustained or stepwise whole-body elevation or descent along the gravity-relative vertical direction within a window.

levels.Low: Little or no sustained vertical progression.
levels.High: Prominent sustained or repeatedly accumulating vertical progression.

attributes.name: airborne_loading_cycle
attributes.definition: Prominence of a recurring motion sequence containing reduced-support or ballistic intervals followed by abrupt landing or loading transients.

levels.Low: No clear reduced-support and landing sequence.
levels.Medium: Occasional or moderately expressed reduced-support and loading sequences.
levels.High: Pronounced and repeatedly expressed reduced-support and landing cycles.

attributes.name: lower_limb_motion_prominence
attributes.definition: Degree to which persistent dynamic motion at the ankle and lower limb is prominent relative to trunk and upper-limb motion.

levels.Low: Little lower-limb motion or motion dominated by the trunk or upper limb.
levels.Medium: Substantial lower-limb motion without clear lower-limb dominance.
levels.High: Persistent motion strongly dominated by the lower limb.

operations.reason: Overall motion energy preserves the principal semantic ordering from static postures through walking to vigorous stair climbing, jogging, running, and jumping.
Repetition rate remains independent of motion magnitude and transfers the gait-speed continuum represented by walking, running, and cycling.
Sustained rapid fluctuation distinguishes vigorous gait and jumping from smooth static or controlled movement without duplicating isolated impact magnitude.
Peak-like impacts provide a transferable contrast between supported gait and more forceful running or jumping while remaining distinct from sustained roughness.

Gravity-relative global inclination is the supported primary distinction among standing still, sitting and relaxing, and lying down, and also represents the forward-inclined configuration associated with stair climbing.
Time-varying gravity-relative configuration distinguishes fixed postures and level gait from activities with appreciable whole-body postural change.
Angular-motion prominence remains a distinct and observable complement to linear progression, with transferable locomotor and articulated-motion anchors.

Generic translation conflates level locomotion with gravity-aligned elevation. Separating these components gives climbing stairs an additional physically meaningful distinction from walking and jogging while horizontal progression retains the shared locomotor relation.
The supplied class semantics assign High motion_regularity to every activity, so it creates no split-specific class contrast despite being physically measurable.

A recurring reduced-support-to-landing sequence is distinct from generic intensity and isolated peak magnitude. It adds a supported gait-regime contrast for jogging versus walking or climbing stairs, transferred from running and jump front & back.

The ankle, chest, and lower-arm inventory can support a body-region motion contrast. Lower-limb prominence links unseen locomotor activities to walking, cycling, and running while separating them from upper-limb-dominant frontal elevation of arms.

semantic_redundancy_review: The final attributes represent distinct physical questions: total motion energy, repetition rate, sustained rapid fluctuation, isolated impacts, mean global inclination, change in global posture, angular-motion prominence, horizontal progression, vertical progression, reduced-support-to-landing sequencing, and lower-limb regional prominence. Smoothness and impulsiveness are retained separately because sustained fluctuation and peak transients are not equivalent. Airborne_loading_cycle describes an ordered temporal pattern rather than impact magnitude alone. Posture_inclination and posture_variability separate mean configuration from within-window change. Horizontal_progression and vertical_progression are gravity-relative components of the former generic translation concept. Lower_limb_motion_prominence concerns where motion is expressed rather than its total magnitude. No second static-posture attribute is added because the supplied capabilities do not justify an independent load-support distinction beyond observable gravity-relative posture.

_meta.validation: Semantic schema and complete A1-to-A2 lineage validated; no feature binding performed.
